newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics reports record earnings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics reports record earnings.

text.p: Modem maker U.S. Robotics Corp. reported a 66 percent increase in fiscal first-quarter profits on Tuesday to a record $69 million, crediting the rise to strong demand for its products.
The earnings, equal to 72 cents per share, compared with year-ago first-quarter profits of $41.7 million, or 45 cents a share.
Skokie, Ill.-based U.S. Robotics also posted a 77 percent rise in revenue, to a record $645.4 million from $364.8 million in the last first quarter.

"Demand continues to be strong for our expanding portfolio of information access products," including the company's Sportster modems and Pilot portable organisers, Chief Operating Officer John McCartney said in a statement.
McCartney said the company expected demand for all its product lines to continue to grow substantially during the rest of the fiscal year.

However, he warned later in a conference call that its results in its current second quarter are heavily dependent on how quickly Internet service providers make available Internet access based on U.S. Robotics's new "x2" technology.
The company reported its results after the stock market closed. Earlier, U.S. Robotics stock dropped 37.5 cents to $73.625.
